title: Tank drive
summary: One stick per side: your first driving code.

say.never: In **tank drive** each stick runs one side of the robot, just like a real tank has two tracks. Left stick runs the left wheels, right stick runs the right wheels.
say.bit: Like a tank: the left stick runs the left side, the right stick runs the right side.

say.never: Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `Robot`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `Robot` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

say.never: Find where it goes. Click in the code, then hold **Ctrl** and tap **F** to open the search box. Type `teleopPeriodic` and press **Enter**. The editor scrolls to the right spot and highlights it.
say.bit: Find where it goes. Press **Ctrl+F**, type `teleopPeriodic` and press Enter to jump to it.

say.never: Now type those three lines in. They go inside `teleopPeriodic()`, **between its curly braces `{` and `}`**. Anything between those braces runs over and over while you drive.
say.bit: Write those three lines inside `teleopPeriodic()`, between its braces.

say.never: Your code only works once it's started. Press **Start** and wait until the status says **Running**.
say.bit: Your code only runs once it's built and started.

hint.never: press Start, then wait for Running.
hint.bit: press Start and wait for Running.

say.never: Choose **Teleop**, then press **Enable**. The robot stays frozen until it's enabled.
say.bit: Pick **Teleop** and press **Enable**. Robot code runs only while it's enabled.

say.never: Drive! **W** and **S** move the left side. The **up and down arrow keys** move the right side. Push one forward and pull the other back and the robot spins on the spot.
say.bit: **W / S** move the left side, **Arrow Up / Down** the right side. Push one forward and one back to spin in place.

say.never: Let's *see* what your code is telling the motors. In **AdvantageScope**, type `LeftOutput` in the search box, then drag **Drive/LeftOutput** onto the graph's **Left Axis**. Now wiggle the keys and watch the line move.
say.bit: See what you're sending to the motors. In AdvantageScope, search for `LeftOutput`, then drag **Drive/LeftOutput** onto the **Left Axis**.
